nanoid keeps each public module as one file named after it: format.js, random.js, generate.js and url.js at the package root, non-secure/generate.js, and async/format.js, async/generate.js and async/random.js, with browser and React Native builds beside them (format.browser.js, random.browser.js, async/format.browser.js, async/random.browser.js, async/random.rn.js). Move each of these thirteen files into a directory named after its module, as index.js, index.browser.js or index.rn.js, with behaviour unchanged: format.js to format/index.js, format.browser.js to format/index.browser.js, random.js to random/index.js, random.browser.js to random/index.browser.js, generate.js to generate/index.js, url.js to url/index.js, non-secure/generate.js to non-secure/generate/index.js, async/format.js to async/format/index.js, async/format.browser.js to async/format/index.browser.js, async/generate.js to async/generate/index.js, async/random.js to async/random/index.js, async/random.browser.js to async/random/index.browser.js, and async/random.rn.js to async/random/index.rn.js. index.js, index.browser.js, async/index.js, async/index.browser.js and non-secure/index.js stay where they are. Leave nothing at the old paths (no re-exporting stubs), and do not change the moved code apart from the module paths in its require calls. Update every reference to an old path: the relative requires between the modules, the requires in the tests under test/, and in package.json the browser field (which maps each Node file to its browser build), the react-native field (the same for React Native) and the size-limit entries, so that each names the moved files with the same mappings and the same limits. Change nothing else in package.json (scripts, jest, eslintConfig, eslintIgnore and every other field stay exactly as they are) and add no other configuration file. What must not change: require("nanoid") and every subpath (format, random, generate, url, non-secure, non-secure/generate, async, async/format, async/generate, async/random) still resolve, now to the moved modules, and export exactly what they export today; a bundler that applies the browser or react-native field gets the same browser and React Native builds as today; ESLint (npx eslint ., which passes on the base) lints each moved file with the rules its old path got and ignores none of them; and every existing test still runs and passes. The tests are Jest files under test/. The project's tests run with npx jest (npm test also runs jest-ci with a 100% coverage threshold, eslint-ci, size-limit and a yarn spelling check; on the unchanged base under this install the coverage threshold is already missed, so those steps are not part of the required test command).

Visible acceptance check (it must pass; it is not the only criterion): node acceptance/visible/check.mjs
The project's own tests run with: npx jest
Deliverables, all required; the task is not done until each is in the tree:
1. The implementation of the behaviour described above, in the project's own source.
2. Regression tests: at least one new test case, in the project's own test directory and style, that fails on the current code and passes with your change, adding at least one new assertion. A change without a new test is incomplete.
3. The visible acceptance check (node acceptance/visible/check.mjs) and the project's own test command (npx jest) both passing on the final tree.
Allowed changes: implementation code, and regression tests for the change (new test files, or new cases added to existing test files, in the project's own test directory and style).
Do not modify anything under acceptance/visible/.
Do not change how the project's checks run: leave the test and coverage configuration files (.taprc*, .nycrc*, .c8rc*, .mocharc*, jest.config.*, vitest.config.*, ava.config.*, karma.conf.*) and the test, pretest and posttest scripts and runner sections of package.json as they are.
Do not delete or weaken existing tests: keep every existing assertion (it may move to another test file), add no skip, only or todo markers, and add no coverage-ignore pragmas. A change that does any of these is rejected at evaluation whatever else passes.
